title: 人間工学
subtitle: Ergonomics
keywords: Human Characteristics 2.Stress and Mental Workload 3.Man-machine System 4.Universal Design and Universal Experience 5.Human Error and Countermeasures
educationalGoal: Ergonomics is a discipline aiming to understand the relationships among humans, products, and the environment that is based on and suited to human characteristics. Students learn human various characteristics, and the basic theories and methodology to design work systems, work environments, and products based on human characteristics.
advice: This course is required for Certified Psychologists. The following topics will be covered: 1. Characteristics of human physiology, psychology, and body 2. Stress and mental workload (MWL) in the work environment 3. Man-machine interface 4. Individual differences 5. Universal design and user experience 6. Human error and countermeasures
requiredKnowledge: Review the contents of previous lectures on psychology, especially Introduction to Psychology, thoroughly.

activityGoals.body: Ability to understand human characteristics and design method based on these characteristics.
Ability to understand human stress and its meaning.
Ability to understand the differences between UD and UX.

achievementLevels.ideal: Ability to understand human characteristics and consider the relationships among humans, products, and the environment. Ability to use knowledge of ergonomics in the field of manufacturing.
achievementLevels.standard: Ability to understand and explain ergonomics from a psychological viewpoint.

lessons.content: Course introduction. The role and significance of ergonomics History of ergonomics
Lecture on ergonomics by an external lecturer working in industry. Explanation of the problem to work on in each self-check.
Human physical characteristics. Dimensions, shape, range of motion, etc. Creating design specifications using percentiles. Writing report 1.
Human psychological characteristics. Sensation and Perception Psychophysics
Human physiological characteristics. Autonomic nerve activity Individual differences.
Stress and MWL. Stress and how to deal with it Questionnaire survey on stress
Return of midterm test. Man-machine interface and individual differences. Relationship between machine and human and individual differences lurking there
Barrier-free and UD. Understanding the differences
UD and UX (I) From the viewpoint of human-centered design
UD and UX (II) Understanding the differences Writing report 2.
Human error. Models of human error Countermeasures Writing report 3.
Lecture by an external lecturer. Final presentation to an external lecturer on the results of self-check activities. Writing report 4. Return of final test.
